verses.1:1: The revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to make plain to His servants, the things that must take place soon; and He signified it, sending through His angel to His servant John,
verses.1:2: who bore witness to the word of God, and to the testimony of Jesus Christ, whatever he saw.
verses.1:3: Blessed is the one who reads and hears the words of this prophecy, and keeps the things that are written in it, for the time is near.
verses.1:4: John to the seven churches that are in Asia. Grace to you and peace from Him who is, and who was, and who is to come, and from the seven spirits who are in the presence of His throne,
verses.1:5: and from Jesus Christ, who is the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the prince of the kings of the earth, who loved us and washed us from our sins in His blood,
verses.1:6: and made us a kingdom and priests to God and His Father: to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
verses.1:7: Look, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye will see Him, and those who pierced Him. And all the tribes of the earth will lament over Him. Yes, amen.
verses.1:8: "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end," says the Lord God, who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty.
verses.1:9: I, John, your brother and sharer in the tribulation and kingdom and endurance in Christ Jesus, was on the island that is called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
verses.1:10: I was in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice like that of a trumpet,
verses.1:11: saying, "Write in a book what you see, and send it to the seven churches that are in Asia: to Ephesus, and to Smyrna, and to Pergamum, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea."
verses.1:12: And I turned to see the voice that was speaking with me; and having turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,
verses.1:13: and in the midst of the seven golden lampstands, one like a Son of Man, clothed in a full-length robe and belted across the chest with a golden sash.
verses.1:14: Now His head and hair were bright white like white wool, and like snow, and His eyes were like a flame of fire;
verses.1:15: and His feet were like fine brass, as in a burning furnace, and His voice was like the sound of many waters;
verses.1:16: and He had seven stars in His right hand, and from His mouth came a sword sharp on both sides, and His face was as the sun shines in its strength.
verses.1:17: And when I saw Him, I fell at His feet as one dead. And He placed His right hand on me, saying, "Do not be afraid; I am the first and the last,
verses.1:18: and the living One; and I was dead, and look, I am living forever and ever, and I have the keys of death and of the underworld.
verses.1:19: Write therefore what you have seen, and the things that are, and the things that must take place after these.
verses.1:20: The mystery of the seven stars that you saw in My right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are the angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are the seven churches."
verses.2:1: "To the angel of the church of Ephesus write: These things says the One who holds the seven stars in His right hand, who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands:
verses.2:2: I know your works, and labor, and your endurance, and that you cannot bear evil people, and you have tested those who say that they are apostles and are not, and have found them to be liars;
verses.2:3: and you have endurance, and have borne up for the sake of My name, and have not grown faint.
verses.2:4: But I have this against you, that you have abandoned your first love.
verses.2:5: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent, and do the first works; but if not, I am coming to you, and I will move your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
verses.2:6: But you have this, that you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
verses.2:7: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches: To the one who conquers, I will grant to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of My God.
verses.2:8: And to the angel of the church of Smyrna write: These things says the first and the last, who was dead and lives:
verses.2:9: I know your tribulation and your poverty, yet you are rich; and you are slandered by those who say that they are Jews and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.
verses.2:10: Fear none of these things that you are about to suffer. Look, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison so that you may be tested, and you will have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
verses.2:11: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches: The one who conquers will not be harmed by the second death.
verses.2:12: And to the angel of the church of Pergamum write: These things says the One who has the broadsword sharp on both sides:
verses.2:13: I know where you dwell, where the seat of Satan is; and you hold fast to My name, and did not deny My faith. And in those days Antipas was My faithful witness, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells.
verses.2:14: But I have a few things against you: because you have there those who hold the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to put a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat and to commit fornication;
verses.2:15: so you also have those who hold the teaching of the Nicolaitans.
verses.2:16: Likewise repent; otherwise I will come to you soon, and I will fight against them with the sword of My mouth.
verses.2:17: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches: To the one who conquers, I will give the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and on the stone a new name written, which no one knows except the one who receives it.
verses.2:18: And to the angel of the church of Thyatira write: These things says the Son of God, who has eyes like a flame of fire, and His feet are like fine brass:
verses.2:19: I know your works, and faith, and your love, and service, and your endurance, and that your last works are more than the first.
verses.2:20: But I have a few things against you: because you allow the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, to teach and to lead My servants astray, to commit fornication and to eat of things sacrificed to idols.
verses.2:21: And I gave her time to repent, and she is unwilling to repent of her fornication.
verses.2:22: Look, I will cast her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her will be in the greatest tribulation, unless they repent of their works.
verses.2:23: And I will kill her children with death, and all the churches will know that I am the One who searches the inward parts and hearts, and I will give to each one of you according to his works. Now to you I say,
verses.2:24: and to the rest who are in Thyatira, all who do not have this teaching, and who have not known the depths of Satan, as they say: I will not lay upon you any other burden;
verses.2:25: nevertheless, hold fast to what you have until I come.
verses.2:26: And the one who conquers and keeps My works until the end, to him I will give authority over the nations,
verses.2:27: and he will rule them with an iron rod, and like a potter's vessel they will be shattered,
verses.2:28: just as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.
verses.2:29: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.3:1: "And to the angel of the church of Sardis write: These things says the One who has the seven spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, and you are dead.
verses.3:2: Be watchful, and strengthen the remaining things that were about to die; for I do not find your works complete before My God.
verses.3:3: Keep in mind therefore how you received and heard, and keep it, and repent. If therefore you do not keep watch, I will come to you like a thief, and you will not know at what hour I will come to you.
verses.3:4: Yet you have a few names in Sardis who have not soiled their garments, and they will walk with Me in white, because they are worthy.
verses.3:5: The one who conquers will thus be clothed in white garments, and I will not erase his name from the book of life, and I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
verses.3:6: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
verses.3:7: And to the angel of the church of Philadelphia write: These things says the Holy One and the True One, who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts, shuts and no one opens:
verses.3:8: I know your works. Look, I have set before you an open door that no one can shut, because you have little strength, and have kept My word, and have not denied My name.
verses.3:9: Look, I will give some from the synagogue of Satan, who say that they are Jews and are not, but lie; look, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and they will know that I have loved you.
verses.3:10: Because you have kept the word of My endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of testing that is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth.
verses.3:11: Look, I am coming soon; hold fast to what you have, so that no one may take your crown.
verses.3:12: The one who conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he will go outside no more; and I will write on him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which comes down from heaven from My God, and My new name.
verses.3:13: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.
verses.3:14: And to the angel of the church of Laodicea write: These things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, who is the beginning of the creation of God:
verses.3:15: I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot; if only you were cold or hot!
verses.3:16: But because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will begin to vomit you out of My mouth,
verses.3:17: because you say, 'I am rich, and made wealthy, and have need of nothing,' and you do not know that you are wretched, and pitiable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
verses.3:18: I advise you to buy from Me gold fired and proven, so that you may become wealthy, and may be clothed in white garments, and the shame of your nakedness may not appear; and anoint your eyes with eye salve so that you may see.
verses.3:19: Those whom I love, I reprove and discipline. Be zealous therefore, and repent.
verses.3:20: Look, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door to Me, I will go in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
verses.3:21: The one who conquers, I will grant him to sit with Me on My throne, just as I also conquered and sat down with My Father on His throne.
verses.3:22: Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.4:1: After these things I looked, and see, an open door in heaven, and the first voice, which I heard like that of a trumpet speaking with me, saying, "Come up here, and I will show you the things that must take place after these things."
verses.4:2: And immediately I was in the Spirit, and look, a throne was set in heaven, and One seated upon the throne.
verses.4:3: And He who was seated was like the appearance of a jasper stone and a sardius, and a rainbow was around the throne, like the appearance of an emerald.
verses.4:4: And around the throne were twenty-four seats, and on the thrones twenty-four elders seated, robed in white garments, and on their heads were golden crowns.
verses.4:5: And from the throne were proceeding flashes of lightning, and voices, and peals of thunder; and seven lamps were burning before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God.
verses.4:6: And in front of the throne was something like a sea of glass, resembling crystal; and in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living beings, full of eyes in front and behind.
verses.4:7: And the first living being was like a lion, and the second living being was like a calf, and the third living being had a face like that of a man, and the fourth living being was like a flying eagle.
verses.4:8: And the four living beings, each one of them had six wings, and all around and within they are full of eyes; and they had no rest day and night, saying, "Holy, Holy, Holy, the Lord God Almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come."
verses.4:9: And whenever those living beings gave glory, and honor, and blessing to Him who sits on the throne, who lives forever and ever,
verses.4:10: the twenty-four elders fell down before Him who sits on the throne, and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying,
verses.4:11: "Worthy are You, Lord our God, to receive glory, and honor, and power, because You created all things, and because of Your will they existed and were created."
verses.5:1: And I saw in the right hand of Him who sits on the throne a scroll written inside and outside, sealed with seven seals.
verses.5:2: And I saw a strong angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?"
verses.5:3: And no one in heaven, or on earth, or under the earth, was able to open the scroll or to look at it.
verses.5:4: And I was weeping greatly, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to see it.
verses.5:5: And one of the elders said to me, "Do not weep; look, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered so as to open the scroll and break its seven seals."
verses.5:6: And I saw, and look, in the midst of the throne and of the four living beings, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though killed, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent into all the earth.
verses.5:7: And He came and took the scroll from the right hand of Him who sits on the throne.
verses.5:8: And when He had opened the scroll, the four living beings and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each one having a harp and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
verses.5:9: And they were singing a new song, saying, "Worthy are You, Lord, to take the scroll and to open its seals, because You were killed, and You redeemed us to God by Your blood from every tribe, and language, and people, and nation,
verses.5:10: and You made us a kingdom and priests to our God, and we will reign on the earth."
verses.5:11: And I looked, and I heard the voice of many angels around the throne, and the living beings, and the elders, and their number was thousands of thousands,
verses.5:12: saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the Lamb who was killed to receive power, and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honor, and glory, and blessing."
verses.5:13: And every creature that is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and those that are in the sea, and those in it, I heard them all saying, "To Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing, and honor, and glory, and authority forever and ever."
verses.5:14: And the four living beings were saying, "Amen." And the twenty-four elders fell down on their faces and worshiped Him who lives forever and ever.
verses.6:1: And I saw that the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living beings saying, as with a voice of thunder, "Come and see."
verses.6:2: And I looked, and see, a white horse; and the one who sat on it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering so that he might conquer.
verses.6:3: And when He had opened the second seal, I heard the second living being saying, "Come and see."
verses.6:4: And another horse, a red one, went out; and to the one who sat on it, it was given to take peace from the earth and that they should kill one another, and a great sword was given to him.
verses.6:5: And when He had opened the third seal, I heard the third living being saying, "Come and see." And look, a black horse; and the one who sat on it had a pair of scales in his hand.
verses.6:6: And I heard something like a voice in the midst of the four living beings saying, "A two-pound measure of wheat for a denarius, and three two-pound measures of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the wine and the oil."
verses.6:7: And when He had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living being saying, "Come and see."
verses.6:8: And look, a pale horse; and the one who sat on it, his name was Death, and the underworld was following him; and authority was given to him over the four parts of the earth, to kill with the sword, with famine, and with death, and by the beasts of the earth.
verses.6:9: And when He had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar the souls of those who had been killed because of the word of God and because of the testimony that they had.
verses.6:10: And they were crying out with a loud voice, saying, "How long, Lord, holy and true, do You not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?"
verses.6:11: And a white robe was given to each of them, and it was told to them that they should rest a little while longer, until their fellow servants and their brothers, who are to be killed just as they also were, are made complete.
verses.6:12: And I looked when He had opened the sixth seal, and see, a great earthquake occurred, and the sun became black like sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood.
verses.6:13: And the stars from the sky fell onto the earth, just as a fig tree casts off its unripe figs when it is shaken by a great wind.
verses.6:14: And the sky receded like a scroll rolled up, and every mountain and the islands were moved from their places.
verses.6:15: And the kings of the earth, and the princes, and the tribunes, and the rich, and the strong, and every slave and free person hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains.
verses.6:16: And they say to the mountains and to the rocks, "Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,
verses.6:17: because the great day of Their wrath has come, and who will be able to stand?"
verses.7:1: After these things I saw four angels standing on the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth so that they would not blow on the earth, nor on the sea, nor against any tree.
verses.7:2: And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, having the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea,
verses.7:3: saying, "Do not harm the earth and the sea, nor the trees, until we seal the servants of our God on their foreheads."
verses.7:4: And I heard the number of those sealed: one hundred forty-four thousand who were sealed, from every tribe of the sons of Israel.
verses.7:5: From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand sealed;
verses.7:6: from the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand sealed;
verses.7:7: from the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand sealed;
verses.7:8: from the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand sealed; from the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.
verses.7:9: After these things I saw a great crowd, which no one could count, from all nations, and tribes, and peoples, and languages, standing before the throne and in the sight of the Lamb, clothed in white robes, and palm branches were in their hands;
verses.7:10: and they were crying out with a loud voice, saying, "Salvation to our God, who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb."
verses.7:11: And all the angels were standing around the throne, and the elders, and the four living creatures; and they fell on their faces in the sight of the throne and worshiped God,
verses.7:12: saying, "Amen. Blessing, and splendor, and wisdom, and thanksgiving, honor, and might, and strength to our God forever and ever. Amen."
verses.7:13: And one of the elders answered and said to me, "These who are clothed in white robes, who are they? And where have they come from?"
verses.7:14: And I said to him, "My lord, you know." And he said to me, "These are the ones who have come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes and whitened them in the blood of the Lamb.
verses.7:15: Therefore they are before the throne of God, and they serve Him day and night in His temple; and He who sits on the throne will dwell over them.
verses.7:16: They will not hunger, nor thirst any longer, nor will the sun fall upon them, nor any scorching heat,
verses.7:17: because the Lamb, who is in the center of the throne, will guide them and lead them to the springs of the waters of life, and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes."
verses.8:1: And when He had opened the seventh seal, there came to be silence in heaven for about half an hour.
verses.8:2: And I saw seven angels standing in the sight of God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
verses.8:3: And another angel came and stood before the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, so that he might offer from the prayers of all the saints on the golden altar that is before the throne of God.
verses.8:4: And the smoke of the incense from the prayers of the saints ascended from the hand of the angel before God.
verses.8:5: And the angel took the censer, and filled it from the fire of the altar, and threw it onto the earth; and there came thunders, and voices, and flashes of lightning, and a great earthquake.
verses.8:6: And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound the trumpet.
verses.8:7: And the first angel sounded the trumpet, and there came hail and fire, mixed in blood, and it was thrown onto the earth; and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees were burned completely, and all green grass was burned up.
verses.8:8: And the second angel sounded the trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was thrown into the sea, and a third of the sea became blood,
verses.8:9: and a third of the creatures, those in the sea that had life, died, and a third of the ships perished.
verses.8:10: And the third angel sounded the trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, burning like a torch, and it fell on a third of the rivers and on the springs of waters;
verses.8:11: and the name of the star is called Wormwood; and a third of the waters turned into wormwood, and many of the people died from the waters, because they had become bitter.
verses.8:12: And the fourth angel sounded the trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them was darkened, and a third of the day did not shine, and likewise of the night.
verses.8:13: And I looked, and I heard the voice of one eagle flying through the middle of heaven, saying with a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell on the earth, because of the remaining voices of the three angels who were about to sound the trumpet."
verses.9:1: And the fifth angel sounded the trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven onto the earth, and the key of the pit of the abyss was given to him.
verses.9:2: And he opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke of the pit ascended, like the smoke of a great furnace, and the sun and the air were darkened from the smoke of the pit.
verses.9:3: And from the smoke of the pit locusts came out onto the earth, and power was given to them, just as the scorpions of the earth have power.
verses.9:4: And it was commanded to them not to injure the grass of the earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree, except only the people who do not have the seal of God on their foreheads.
verses.9:5: And it was given to them not to kill them, but to torment them for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a person.
verses.9:6: And in those days people will seek death and will not find it; and they will long to die, and death will flee from them.
verses.9:7: And the likenesses of the locusts were like horses prepared for battle; and on their heads were things like crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like the faces of human beings.
verses.9:8: And they had hair like the hair of women. And their teeth were like the teeth of lions.
verses.9:9: And they had breastplates like iron breastplates, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots of many horses running into war.
verses.9:10: And they had tails like those of scorpions, and stingers were in their tails, and their power was to harm people for five months.
verses.9:11: And they had over themselves as king the angel of the abyss, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek Apollyon, having in Latin the name Exterminans.
verses.9:12: One woe has passed, and look, two woes are still coming after these things.
verses.9:13: And the sixth angel sounded the trumpet, and I heard one voice from the four horns of the golden altar that is before the eyes of God,
verses.9:14: saying to the sixth angel who had the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound in the great river Euphrates."
verses.9:15: And the four angels were released, who were prepared for the hour, and day, and month, and year, to kill a third of the people.
verses.9:16: And the number of the mounted army was twenty thousand times ten thousand. And I heard their number.
verses.9:17: And thus I saw the horses in the vision: and those who sat on them had fiery, and hyacinth, and sulfurous breastplates, and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions; and from their mouths proceeds fire, and smoke, and sulfur.
verses.9:18: And by these three plagues a third of the people were killed, from the fire, and from the smoke, and the sulfur that were proceeding from their mouths.
verses.9:19: For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with these they do harm.
verses.9:20: And the rest of the people, who were not killed in these plagues, did not even repent of the works of their hands, so that they would not worship demons, and images of gold, and of silver, and of bronze, and of stone, and of wood, which can neither see, nor hear, nor walk;
verses.9:21: and they did not repent from their murders, nor from their sorceries, nor from their fornication, nor from their thefts.
verses.10:1: And I saw another strong angel descending from heaven, clothed in a cloud, and a rainbow was on his head, and his face was like the sun, and his feet were like pillars of fire.
verses.10:2: And he had in his hand a small open book, and he placed his right foot on the sea, and his left on the earth.
verses.10:3: And he cried out with a loud voice, just as when a lion roars. And when he had cried out, seven thunders spoke their voices.
verses.10:4: And when the seven thunders had spoken their voices, I was about to write; and I heard a voice from heaven saying to me, "Seal up the things that the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them down."
verses.10:5: And the angel whom I saw standing on the sea and on the earth raised his hand to heaven.
verses.10:6: And he swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it, and the earth and the things that are in it, and the sea and the things that are in it, that time will be no longer,
verses.10:7: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he begins to sound the trumpet, the mystery of God will be completed, just as He proclaimed the good news through His servants the prophets.
verses.10:8: And I heard the voice from heaven speaking with me again and saying, "Go and take the open book from the hand of the angel standing on the sea and on the earth."
verses.10:9: And I went to the angel, telling him to give me the book. And he said to me, "Take the book and devour it; and it will make your stomach bitter, but in your mouth it will be sweet like honey."
verses.10:10: And I took the book from the hand of the angel and devoured it, and in my mouth it was sweet like honey; and when I had devoured it, my stomach turned bitter.
verses.10:11: And he said to me, "You must prophesy again to nations and peoples and languages and many kings."
verses.11:1: And a reed like a rod was given to me, and it was said to me, "Rise and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
verses.11:2: But cast out the court that is outside the temple, and do not measure it, because it has been given to the nations, and they will trample the holy city for forty-two months.
verses.11:3: And I will give to My two witnesses, and they will prophesy for one thousand two hundred sixty days, clothed in sackcloth."
verses.11:4: These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing in the presence of the Lord of the earth.
verses.11:5: And if anyone wants to harm them, fire will come out from their mouth and devour their enemies; and if anyone wants to injure them, in this way he must be killed.
verses.11:6: These have authority to shut the sky so that it may not rain in the days of their prophecy, and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they wish.
verses.11:7: And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that ascends from the abyss will wage war against them, and will conquer them, and will kill them.
verses.11:8: And their bodies will lie in the streets of the great city, which is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord also was crucified.
verses.11:9: And some from the tribes and peoples and languages and nations will look at their bodies for three and a half days, and they will not allow their bodies to be placed in tombs.
verses.11:10: And the inhabitants of the earth will rejoice over them and celebrate, and they will send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who lived on the earth.
verses.11:11: And after three and a half days, the spirit of life from God entered into them. And they stood on their feet, and great fear fell upon those who saw them.
verses.11:12: And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, "Come up here." And they ascended into heaven in a cloud, and their enemies saw them.
verses.11:13: And in that hour a great earthquake took place, and a tenth part of the city fell, and seven thousand persons were killed in the earthquake; and the rest were thrown into fear and gave glory to the God of heaven.
verses.11:14: The second woe has passed; and look, the third woe will come soon.
verses.11:15: And the seventh angel sounded the trumpet, and loud voices arose in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of this world has become that of our Lord and of His Christ, and He will reign forever and ever. Amen."
verses.11:16: And the twenty-four elders, who sit on their seats in the presence of God, fell on their faces and worshiped God, saying,
verses.11:17: "We give thanks to You, Lord God Almighty, who are, and who were, and who are to come, because You have taken Your great power and reigned.
verses.11:18: And the nations grew angry, and Your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to give the reward to Your servants the prophets, and to the saints, and to those who fear Your name, small and great, and to destroy those who have corrupted the earth."
verses.11:19: And the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant was seen in His temple; and there came flashes of lightning, and voices, and an earthquake, and great hail.
verses.12:1: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman clothed in the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and a crown of twelve stars on her head.
verses.12:2: And being pregnant, she was crying out in labor and was in torment to give birth.
verses.12:3: And another sign was seen in heaven: and look, a great red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and on his heads seven diadems.
verses.12:4: And his tail dragged a third part of the stars of heaven and cast them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she had given birth, he might devour her son.
verses.12:5: And she gave birth to a male son, who was to rule all the nations with an iron rod; and her son was caught up to God and to His throne.
verses.12:6: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she had a place prepared by God, so that there they might feed her for one thousand two hundred sixty days.
verses.12:7: And a great battle took place in heaven: Michael and his angels battled with the dragon, and the dragon fought, and his angels.
verses.12:8: And they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them any longer in heaven.
verses.12:9: And that great dragon was thrown down, the ancient serpent, who is called the devil and Satan, who deceives the whole world; and he was thrown down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.
verses.12:10: And I heard a loud voice in heaven saying, "Now have come the salvation, and the power, and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ, because the accuser of our brothers has been thrown down, who accused them in the presence of our God day and night.
verses.12:11: And they themselves conquered him on account of the blood of the Lamb and on account of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives even to death.
verses.12:12: Therefore rejoice, heavens, and you who dwell in them. Woe to the earth and to the sea, because the devil has come down to you having great wrath, knowing that he has a short time."
verses.12:13: And after the dragon saw that he had been thrown down to the earth, he pursued the woman who gave birth to the male child.
verses.12:14: And two wings of a great eagle were given to the woman, so that she might fly into the desert, to her place, where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.
verses.12:15: And the serpent cast water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, so that he might cause her to be carried away by the river.
verses.12:16: And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river that the dragon cast from his mouth.
verses.12:17: And the dragon grew angry with the woman, and he went away to do battle with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
verses.12:18: And he stood upon the sand of the sea.
verses.13:1: And I saw a beast rising out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns, and on its horns ten diadems, and on its heads names of blasphemy.
verses.13:2: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion. And the dragon gave to it his power and great authority.
verses.13:3: And I saw one of its heads as if killed to death, and the wound of its death was healed. And the whole earth marveled after the beast.
verses.13:4: And they worshiped the dragon, who gave authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast? And who will be able to fight against it?"
verses.13:5: And a mouth was given to it, speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.
verses.13:6: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tabernacle and those who dwell in heaven.
verses.13:7: And it was granted to it to make war against the saints and to conquer them. And authority was given to it over every tribe and people and language and nation.
verses.13:8: And all who dwell on the earth worshiped it, whose names have not been written in the book of life of the Lamb, who was killed from the beginning of the world.
verses.13:9: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
verses.13:10: Whoever leads into captivity will go into captivity; whoever kills with the sword must be killed by the sword. Here is the endurance and faith of the saints.
verses.13:11: And I saw another beast rising out of the earth, and it had two horns like those of a lamb, and it spoke like a dragon.
verses.13:12: And it exercised all the authority of the former beast in its sight, and it made the earth and those who dwell in it worship the first beast, whose wound of death was healed.
verses.13:13: And it performed great signs, so that it even made fire descend from heaven to the earth in the sight of people.
verses.13:14: And it deceived those who dwell on the earth because of the signs that were given to it to perform in the sight of the beast, telling those who dwell on the earth to make an image of the beast that has the wound of the sword and lived.
verses.13:15: And it was granted to it to give breath to the image of the beast, and so that the image of the beast might speak and cause whoever would not worship the image of the beast to be killed.
verses.13:16: And it will cause all, small and great, and rich and poor, and free and slave, to have a mark on their right hand or on their foreheads,
verses.13:17: and so that no one may be able to buy or sell except the one who has the mark, or the name of the beast, or the number of its name.
verses.13:18: Here is wisdom. Let the one who has understanding calculate the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred sixty-six.
verses.14:1: And I saw, and look: the Lamb was standing on Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred forty-four thousand, having His name and the name of His Father written on their foreheads.
verses.14:2: And I heard a sound from heaven, like the sound of many waters and like the sound of loud thunder, and the sound that I heard was like that of harpists playing on their harps.
verses.14:3: And they were singing, as it were, a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one was able to recite the song except those one hundred forty-four thousand who were bought from the earth.
verses.14:4: These are the ones who have not been defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were bought from among mankind as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,
verses.14:5: and in their mouth no lie was found, for they are without blemish before the throne of God.
verses.14:6: And I saw another angel flying through the middle of heaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who sit on the earth, and to every nation and tribe and language and people,
verses.14:7: saying with a loud voice, "Fear the Lord and give Him honor, because the hour of His judgment has come, and worship Him who made heaven and earth, the sea, and the springs of waters."
verses.14:8: And another angel followed, saying, "Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon, who made all the nations drink from the wine of the wrath of her fornication."
verses.14:9: And a third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice, "If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives a mark on his forehead or on his hand,
verses.14:10: he also will drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is mixed undiluted in the cup of His own wrath, and he will be tormented with fire and sulfur in the sight of the holy angels and before the sight of the Lamb;
verses.14:11: and the smoke of their torments will ascend forever and ever; and they have no rest day and night, those who worshiped the beast and its image, and if anyone receives the mark of its name."
verses.14:12: Here is the endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
verses.14:13: And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me, "Write: 'Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord.'" "From now on, indeed," says the Spirit, "that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow them."
verses.14:14: And I saw, and look: a white cloud, and seated on the cloud one like a Son of Man, having on His head a golden crown, and in His hand a sharp sickle.
verses.14:15: And another angel came out from the temple, crying out with a loud voice to Him who was seated on the cloud, "Send out Your sickle and reap, because the hour has come to reap, since the harvest of the earth has dried."
verses.14:16: And He who was seated on the cloud sent His sickle onto the earth, and the earth was reaped.
verses.14:17: And another angel came out from the temple that is in heaven, also having a sharp sickle himself.
verses.14:18: And another angel came out from the altar, who had authority over fire, and he cried out with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, saying, "Send out your sharp sickle and harvest the clusters of the vineyard of the earth, since its grapes are ripe."
verses.14:19: And the angel sent his sharp sickle onto the earth, and harvested the vineyard of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God,
verses.14:20: and the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out from the winepress up to the bridles of the horses for one thousand six hundred stadia.
verses.15:1: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and astonishing: seven angels having the seven last plagues, since in them the wrath of God has been completed.
verses.15:2: And I saw something like a sea of glass mixed with fire, and those who conquered the beast and its image and the number of its name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God,
verses.15:3: and singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and astonishing are Your works, Lord God Almighty; just and true are Your ways, King of the ages.
verses.15:4: Who will not fear You, Lord, and magnify Your name? For You alone are merciful; for all the nations will come and worship in Your sight, because Your judgments are manifest."
verses.15:5: And after these things I saw, and look: the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened,
verses.15:6: and the seven angels having the seven plagues came out from the temple, clothed in clean and bright white linen, and wrapped around their chests with golden sashes.
verses.15:7: And one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls, full of the fury of God, who lives forever and ever.
verses.15:8: And the temple was filled with smoke from the majesty of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.
verses.16:1: And I heard a loud voice from the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go, and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God onto the earth."
verses.16:2: And the first departed and poured out his bowl onto the earth, and a fierce and malignant wound came upon the people who had the mark of the beast and upon those who worshiped its image.
verses.16:3: And the second angel poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead person, and every living soul died in the sea.
verses.16:4: And the third poured out his bowl upon the rivers and upon the springs of waters, and they became blood.
verses.16:5: And I heard the angel of the waters saying, "You are just, Lord, who are and who were holy, who have judged these things,
verses.16:6: because they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink; for they are deserving."
verses.16:7: And I heard another from the altar saying, "Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are Your judgments."
verses.16:8: And the fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was given to it to afflict people with heat and with fire;
verses.16:9: and people were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has authority over these plagues, nor did they repent so as to give Him glory.
verses.16:10: And the fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the seat of the beast, and its kingdom became dark, and they gnawed their tongues because of pain,
verses.16:11: and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their wounds, and they did not repent from their deeds.
verses.16:12: And the sixth angel poured out his bowl into that great river, the Euphrates, and dried up its water, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun.
verses.16:13: And I saw, out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits in the likeness of frogs.
verses.16:14: For they are spirits of demons performing signs, and they go out to the kings of the whole earth to gather them into battle for the great day of Almighty God.
verses.16:15: "Look, I am coming like a thief. Blessed is the one who keeps watch and guards his garments, so that he does not walk naked and they see his shame."
verses.16:16: And he will gather them into the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.
verses.16:17: And the seventh angel poured out his bowl into the air, and a loud voice came out from the temple, from the throne, saying, "It is done."
verses.16:18: And there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and peals of thunder, and there was a great earthquake, such as never was since people were on the earth, such an earthquake, so great.
verses.16:19: And the great city was turned into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell. And Babylon the great came into remembrance before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the indignation of His wrath.
verses.16:20: And every island fled, and mountains were not found.
verses.16:21: And great hail like a talent came down from heaven upon people, and people blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, because it became extremely great.
verses.17:1: And one of the seven angels who had the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the condemnation of the great prostitute who sits upon many waters,
verses.17:2: with whom the kings of the earth fornicated, and those who inhabit the earth became drunk from the wine of her prostitution."
verses.17:3: And he carried me away in spirit into a desert. And I saw a woman sitting upon a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
verses.17:4: And the woman was clothed in purple and scarlet, and gilded with gold and precious stone and pearls, having a golden cup in her hand, full of abomination and the uncleanness of her fornication.
verses.17:5: And upon her forehead was written a name: "Mystery: Babylon the great, mother of fornications and of the abominations of the earth."
verses.17:6: And I saw the woman drunk from the blood of the saints and from the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. And when I saw her, I marveled with great amazement.
verses.17:7: And the angel said to me, "Why do you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman, and of the beast that carries her, which has seven heads and ten horns.
verses.17:8: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to ascend from the abyss, and will go into destruction; and those who inhabit the earth (whose names are not written in the book of life from the foundation of the world) will marvel, seeing the beast, which was and is not.
verses.17:9: And here is the mind that has wisdom. The seven heads are seven mountains on which the woman sits, and they are seven kings.
verses.17:10: Five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a short time.
verses.17:11: And the beast that was, and is not, it itself is also the eighth, and is of the seven, and goes into destruction.
verses.17:12: And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings, who have not yet received a kingdom, but they will receive authority as kings for one hour after the beast.
verses.17:13: These have one purpose, and they will hand over their power and authority to the beast.
verses.17:14: These will fight against the Lamb, and the Lamb will conquer them, because He is Lord of lords and King of kings, and those who are with Him are called, chosen, and faithful."
verses.17:15: And he said to me, "The waters that you saw, where the prostitute sits, are peoples, and nations, and languages.
verses.17:16: And the ten horns that you saw on the beast, these will hate the prostitute, and will make her desolate and naked, and will eat her flesh, and will burn her up with fire.
verses.17:17: For God has put into their hearts to do what is pleasing to Him, to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God are fulfilled.
verses.17:18: And the woman whom you saw is the great city that holds kingship over the kings of the earth."
verses.18:1: And after these things I saw another angel descending from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was illuminated by his glory.
verses.18:2: And he cried out with strength, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, and she has become a dwelling of demons, and a place of confinement for every unclean spirit, and a place of confinement for every unclean and detestable bird,
verses.18:3: because all nations have drunk from the wine of the wrath of her fornication, and the kings of the earth have fornicated with her, and the merchants of the earth have become rich from the power of her luxury."
verses.18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out from her, My people, so that you do not share in her offenses, and do not receive any of her plagues.
verses.18:5: For her sins have reached as far as heaven, and the Lord has remembered her iniquities.
verses.18:6: Repay her just as she herself has repaid you, and pay back double according to her deeds; in the cup in which she mixed, mix double for her.
verses.18:7: As much as she glorified herself and was in luxury, just as much give her torment and mourning, because in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen, and I am not a widow, and I will not see mourning.'
verses.18:8: Therefore in one day her plagues will come: death, and mourning, and famine, and she will be burned up with fire, because mighty is God, who will judge her."
verses.18:9: And the kings of the earth, who fornicated with her and lived in luxury, will weep and lament over her when they see the smoke of her burning,
verses.18:10: standing far off because of fear of her torments, saying, "Woe, woe, that great city Babylon, that mighty city, because in one hour your judgment has come."
verses.18:11: And the traders of the earth will weep and mourn over her, because no one will buy their merchandise any longer:
verses.18:12: merchandise of gold, and silver, and precious stone, and pearl, and fine linen, and purple, and silk, and scarlet, and all thyine wood, and all vessels of ivory, and all vessels of precious stone, and of bronze, and of iron, and of marble;
verses.18:13: and cinnamon, and spices, and ointment, and frankincense, and wine, and oil, and fine flour, and wheat, and cattle, and sheep, and horses, and carriages, and slaves, and the souls of people.
verses.18:14: And the fruits of the desire of your soul have departed from you, and all rich and splendid things have perished from you, and they will not find them any longer.
verses.18:15: The merchants of these things, who became rich, will stand far off from her because of fear of her torments, weeping and mourning,
verses.18:16: and saying, "Woe, woe, that great city, which was dressed in fine linen, and purple, and scarlet, and was gilded with gold, and precious stone, and pearls,
verses.18:17: because in one hour such great riches have been laid waste." And every helmsman, and everyone who sails on a lake, and sailors, and those who work on the sea, stood far off,
verses.18:18: and cried out, seeing the place of her burning, saying, "What is like this great city?"
verses.18:19: And they threw dust upon their heads, and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying, "Woe, woe, that great city, in which all who had ships on the sea became rich from her prices, because in one hour she has been made desolate."
verses.18:20: Rejoice over her, heaven, and holy apostles and prophets, because God has judged your judgment on her.
verses.18:21: And one mighty angel lifted up a stone like a great millstone and hurled it into the sea, saying, "With this force Babylon, that great city, will be hurled, and will no longer be found.
verses.18:22: And the sound of harpists, and of musicians, and of those playing the flute and the trumpet will not be heard in you any longer; and no craftsman of any craft will be found in you any longer; and the sound of a millstone will not be heard in you any longer;
verses.18:23: and the light of a lamp will not shine in you any longer; and the voice of bridegroom and bride will not be heard in you anymore; because your merchants were the princes of the earth, because in your sorceries all nations went astray.
verses.18:24: And in her was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all who have been killed on the earth."
verses.19:1: After these things I heard something like the voice of many crowds in heaven, saying, "Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,
verses.19:2: because true and just are the judgments of Him who passed judgment on the great prostitute who corrupted the earth through her prostitution, and avenged the blood of His servants from her hands."
verses.19:3: And again they said, "Hallelujah!" And her smoke rises forever and ever.
verses.19:4: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God sitting on the throne, saying, "Amen! Hallelujah!"
verses.19:5: And a voice came out from the throne, saying, "Give praise to our God, all His servants, and you who fear Him, small and great."
verses.19:6: And I heard something like the voice of a great crowd, and like the sound of many waters, and like the sound of great thunders, saying, "Hallelujah! For the Lord our God, the Almighty, has begun to reign.
verses.19:7: Let us rejoice and exult, and let us give glory to Him, because the wedding of the Lamb has come, and His wife has prepared herself."
verses.19:8: And it was given to her to clothe herself with fine linen, shining and bright white; for fine linen is the just deeds of the saints.
verses.19:9: And he said to me, "Write: 'Blessed are those who are called to the wedding supper of the Lamb.'" And he said to me, "These words of God are true."
verses.19:10: And I fell before his feet to worship him. And he says to me, "See that you do not do that! I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brothers who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God. For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."
verses.19:11: And I saw heaven opened, and look, a white horse, and He who sat on it was called Faithful and True, and with justice He judges and fights.
verses.19:12: Now His eyes were like a flame of fire, and on His head were many diadems, and He had a name written that no one knows except Himself.
verses.19:13: And He was clothed in a garment sprinkled with blood, and His name is called the Word of God.
verses.19:14: And the armies that are in heaven were following Him on white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and clean.
verses.19:15: And from His mouth proceeds a sword sharp on both sides, so that with it He may strike the nations. And He Himself will rule them with an iron rod; and He Himself treads the winepress of the wine of the fury of the wrath of God Almighty.
verses.19:16: And on His garment and on His thigh He has written, "King of kings and Lord of those who rule."
verses.19:17: And I saw one angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that were flying through the middle of heaven, "Come and gather together for the great supper of God,
verses.19:18: so that you may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of tribunes, and the flesh of the mighty, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all, free and slave, both small and great."
verses.19:19: And I saw the beast and the kings of the earth and their armies gathered together to wage battle against Him who sat on the horse and against His army.
verses.19:20: And the beast was seized, and with it the false prophet who performed signs in its presence, by which he led astray those who received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. These two were thrown alive into the lake of fire burning with sulfur.
verses.19:21: And the rest were killed by the sword of Him who sat on the horse, which proceeds from His mouth; and all the birds were filled with their flesh.
verses.20:1: And I saw an angel coming down from heaven, having the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand.
verses.20:2: And he seized the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years,
verses.20:3: and threw him into the abyss, and shut it and sealed it over him, so that he would no longer lead the nations astray until the thousand years are completed; and after these things he must be released for a short time.
verses.20:4: And I saw seats, and they sat on them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded because of the testimony of Jesus and because of the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast or its image, nor received its mark on their foreheads or on their hands; and they lived and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
verses.20:5: The rest of the dead did not live until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection.
verses.20:6: Blessed and holy is the one who has a part in the first resurrection. Over these the second death has no power, but they will be priests of God and of Christ, and they will reign with Him for a thousand years.
verses.20:8: And when the thousand years have been completed, Satan will be released from his prison, and he will go out and lead astray the nations that are on the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, and gather them together for battle; their number is like the sand of the sea.
verses.20:9: And they went up over the breadth of the earth and surrounded the camp of the saints and the beloved city.
verses.20:10: And fire came down from God out of heaven and devoured them; and the devil who was leading them astray was thrown into the lake of fire and sulfur, where both the beast and the false prophet will be tormented day and night forever and ever.
verses.20:11: And I saw a great, bright white throne and Him who sat on it, from whose presence earth and heaven fled, and no place was found for them.
verses.20:12: And I saw the dead, great and small, standing before the throne, and books were opened; and another book was opened, which is the book of life; and the dead were judged from the things that were written in the books, according to their works.
verses.20:13: And the sea gave up the dead who were in it, and death and the underworld gave up their dead who were in them; and judgment was passed on each one according to their works.
verses.20:14: And the underworld and death were thrown into the lake of fire. This is the second death.
verses.20:15: And whoever was not found written in the book of life was thrown into the lake of fire.
verses.21:1: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth. For the first heaven and the first earth passed away, and the sea no longer exists.
verses.21:2: And I, John, saw the holy city, the new Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.
verses.21:3: And I heard a loud voice from the throne, saying, "Look, the tabernacle of God is with people, and He will dwell with them. And they themselves will be His people, and God Himself will be with them, their God,
verses.21:4: and God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; and death will be no more, nor will mourning, nor outcry, nor pain exist any longer, because the first things have passed away."
verses.21:5: And He who sat on the throne said, "Look, I am making all things new." And He said to me, "Write, because these words are most faithful and true."
verses.21:6: And He said to me, "It is done! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end. To the one who is thirsty I will give from the spring of the water of life, freely.
verses.21:7: The one who conquers will possess these things, and I will be God to him, and he will be a son to Me.
verses.21:8: But as for the cowardly, and the unbelieving, and the abominable, and murderers, and fornicators, and sorcerers, and idolaters, and all liars, their portion will be in the lake burning with fire and sulfur, which is the second death."
verses.21:9: And one of the seven angels who had the bowls full of the seven last plagues came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, and I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb."
verses.21:10: And he carried me up in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the holy city Jerusalem coming down out of heaven from God,
verses.21:11: having the radiance of God; and its light was like a precious stone, like a jasper stone, like crystal.
verses.21:12: And it had a great and high wall, having twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed, which are the names of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel:
verses.21:13: on the east three gates, and on the north three gates, and on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.
verses.21:14: And the wall of the city had twelve foundations, and on them were the twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
verses.21:15: And the one who was speaking with me had a golden measuring reed to measure the city, and its gates, and the wall.
verses.21:16: And the city is laid out as a square, and its length is as great as its width; and he measured the city with the golden reed at twelve thousand stadia, and its length and height and width are equal.
verses.21:17: And he measured its wall: one hundred forty-four cubits, by human measurement, which is that of an angel.
verses.21:18: And the structure of its wall was of jasper stone, while the city itself was pure gold, like pure glass.
verses.21:19: And the foundations of the wall of the city were adorned with every precious stone. The first foundation was jasper; the second, sapphire; the third, chalcedony; the fourth, emerald;
verses.21:20: the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprase; the eleventh, hyacinth; the twelfth, amethyst.
verses.21:21: And the twelve gates are twelve pearls, one for each; and each single gate was made of a single pearl. And the street of the city was pure gold, like transparent glass.
verses.21:22: And I saw no temple in it, for the Lord God Almighty is its temple, and the Lamb.
verses.21:23: And the city has no need of the sun or the moon to shine in it, for the radiance of God has illuminated it, and its lamp is the Lamb.
verses.21:24: And the nations will walk in its light, and the kings of the earth will bring their glory and honor into it.
verses.21:25: And its gates will not be closed by day, for there will be no night there.
verses.21:26: And they will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.
verses.21:27: Nothing defiled will enter into it, nor anyone who practices abomination and falsehood, except those who are written in the book of life of the Lamb.
verses.22:1: And he showed me a river of the water of life, shining like crystal, issuing from the throne of God and of the Lamb.
verses.22:2: In the middle of its street, and on either side of the river, was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits month by month, yielding its fruit; and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
verses.22:3: And there will be no curse any longer, but the thrones of God and of the Lamb will be in it, and His servants will serve Him.
verses.22:4: And they will see His face, and His name will be on their foreheads.
verses.22:5: And there will be no more night, and they will not need the light of a lamp nor the light of the sun, because the Lord God will illuminate them, and they will reign forever and ever.
verses.22:6: And he said to me, "These words are most faithful and true. And the Lord God of the spirits of the prophets has sent His angel to show His servants the things that must happen soon.
verses.22:7: And look, I am coming swiftly. Blessed is the one who guards the words of the prophecy of this book."
verses.22:8: And I, John, am the one who heard and saw these things. And after I had heard and seen, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who was showing me these things.
verses.22:9: And he said to me, "See that you do not do it, for I am a fellow servant of yours, and of your brothers the prophets, and of those who keep the words of the prophecy of this book. Worship God."
verses.22:10: And he says to me, "Do not seal the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is near.
verses.22:11: Let the one who does harm do harm still, and let the one who is in filth grow filthy still, and let the one who is righteous be justified still, and let the holy one be sanctified still.
verses.22:12: Look, I am coming soon, and My reward is with Me, to repay each one according to his works.
verses.22:13: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the first and the last, the beginning and the end.
verses.22:14: Blessed are those who wash their robes in the blood of the Lamb, so that the right to the tree of life may be theirs and they may enter through the gates into the city.
verses.22:15: Outside are the dogs, and the sorcerers, and the sexually immoral, and the murderers, and those who serve idols, and everyone who loves and practices a lie.
verses.22:16: I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify about these things to you in the churches. I am the root and the offspring of David, the shining morning star."
verses.22:17: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come." And let the one who hears say, "Come." And let the one who thirsts come, and let the one who wishes receive the water of life freely.
verses.22:18: "For I solemnly testify to everyone who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to these things, God will add upon him the plagues written in this book.
verses.22:19: And if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God will remove his share from the book of life, and from the holy city, and from the things that are written in this book,"
verses.22:20: says the One who bears witness to these things. "Yes, I am coming soon." Amen. Come, Lord Jesus.
verses.22:21: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with all of you. Amen.

notes.1:3: The Vulgate uses singular verbs ("reads and hears ... and keeps") rather than switching to the plural ("those who hear ... and keep") as in the Greek text.
notes.1:5: The Vulgate reads "loved" (perfect tense, dilexit) and "washed us" (lavit nos, corresponding to the Greek variant lousanti) rather than "loves" and "freed us" (lysanti).
notes.1:8: The Vulgate includes "the beginning and the end" (principium et finis), a clause omitted in most modern critical Greek editions.
notes.1:15: Latin auricalco denotes a gleaming gold-copper alloy or fine brass; the Vulgate also reads simply "as in a burning furnace" (sicut in camino ardenti) without the Greek participle "refined."
notes.1:18: Latin inferni ("of the underworld," rendering Greek Hades) denotes the realm of the dead, rendered consistently as "the underworld" across Revelation (1:18, 6:8, 20:13-14) and Acts 2:24, 27, 31.
notes.1:20: Latin sacramentum ("sacrament" or "sacred mystery") renders Greek mysterion and here signifies the hidden symbolic meaning of the seven stars and lampstands.
notes.2:5: Latin age poenitentiam (literally "do penance" or "exercise repentance") is the standard Vulgate idiom for repenting, paired with the verb poenitere in 2:21.
notes.2:7: The Vulgate reads "of My God" (Dei mei) rather than simply "of God" as in most modern critical Greek texts.
notes.2:13: The Vulgate clause Et in diebus illis Antipas testis meus fidelis is elliptical and lacks a main verb before the relative clause; "was" is supplied to complete the sentence.
notes.2:14: The Vulgate reads simply "to eat and to commit fornication" (edere, et fornicari), omitting "things sacrificed to idols," which appears in the Greek text and in 2:20.
notes.2:22: The Vulgate reflexive pronoun suis ("their works") refers to those who commit adultery with Jezebel, whereas the Greek text reads "her works" (autes).
notes.3:2: The Vulgate uses the present tense "I do not find" (non ... invenio) rather than the Greek perfect "I have not found," and describes the works as not "complete" (plena, literally "full").
notes.3:14: Although the Clementine edition prints a colon after dicit ("says"), Amen ("the Amen") functions with "the faithful and true witness" as the subject of the clause, matching the Greek title.
notes.3:16: The Vulgate reads "But" (sed) and literally "I will begin to vomit you out" (incipiam te evomere), translating the Greek periphrastic future ("I am about to") with incipiam.
notes.3:20: The Vulgate includes "to Me" (mihi) after "opens the door," a reading absent from most modern critical Greek editions.
notes.4:4: The Vulgate varies the Latin terminology here between sedes ("throne"), sedilia ("seats"), and thronos ("thrones"), whereas the Greek repeats thronos throughout.
notes.4:6: Latin animalia literally denotes "living beings" (creatures endowed with life, anima), rendering Greek zoa ("living creatures").
notes.4:9: Vulgate-distinct reading: "blessing" (benedictionem), whereas the Greek text reads "thanksgiving" (eucharistian).
notes.4:11: Latin Domine Deus noster reads literally "Lord our God," without a conjunction between "Lord" and "God" (contrast Greek "our Lord and our God").
notes.5:1: Latin liber denotes an ancient book-roll or scroll, sealed along its margin and rolled up (cf. 6:14).
notes.5:8: Vulgate-distinct reading: "when He had opened the scroll" (aperuisset), whereas the Greek text reads "when He had taken the scroll" (elaben).
notes.5:9: Notable Vulgate readings in vv. 9-10: the Latin includes "Lord" (Domine), has "open" (aperire) rather than "break/loose" its seals, and reads first-person "us ... we will reign" (nos ... regnabimus) where critical Greek texts omit "us" in v. 9 and read third-person "them ... they will reign" in v. 10.
notes.5:11: Vulgate-distinct reading: "thousands of thousands" (millia millium), omitting the preceding "myriads of myriads" present in the Greek text.
notes.5:12: Notable Vulgate-distinct reading: "divinity" (divinitatem), where the Greek text reads "wealth/riches" (plouton, Latin divitias).
notes.6:1: The Vulgate reads "that the Lamb had opened" (quod aperuisset) rather than "when," and includes "and see" (et vide) here and in vv. 3, 5, and 7, which critical Greek editions omit.
notes.6:6: Latin bilibris is literally a two-pound measure (rendering Greek choinix), and a denarius was a silver coin roughly equal to a day's wage; note also the Vulgate order "the wine and the oil" (Greek: "the oil and the wine").
notes.6:8: Latin infernus ("hell") denotes the underworld or realm of the dead (Greek Hades). Notably, the Clementine Vulgate reads "over the four parts of the earth" (quatuor partes) and singular "to him" (illi), whereas the Greek reads "over a fourth of the earth" and (in critical editions) plural "to them."
notes.6:17: The Vulgate reads plural "Their wrath" (irae ipsorum), referring jointly to God and the Lamb, whereas critical Greek editions read singular "His wrath."
notes.7:5: Unlike many Greek manuscripts that include 'sealed' only on the first and last tribes, the Clementine Vulgate repeats signati ('sealed') for all twelve tribes in 7:5-8.
notes.7:15: Vulgate habitabit super illos literally reads 'will dwell over them,' where the Greek text uses a verb meaning 'will spread His tent/tabernacle over them.'
notes.7:17: Vulgate reget ('will guide/rule') corresponds to Greek poimanei ('will shepherd'), and vitae fontes aquarum preserves the plural 'waters' ('springs of the waters of life').
notes.8:3: Vulgate de orationibus ('from/of the prayers') in 8:3-4 uses a preposition of source/partitive sense rather than the Greek dative ('with/to the prayers'), and 8:3 uniquely adds Dei ('of God') after 'throne.'
notes.8:5: The Clementine Vulgate orders the phenomena as 'thunders, and voices, and flashes of lightning' and adds magnus ('a great earthquake'), where Greek manuscripts generally read simply 'an earthquake.'
notes.8:9: Latin creaturae eorum, quae habebant animas literally reads 'of the creation of those that had living souls/life,' with animas denoting vital life or living souls.
notes.8:13: Vulgate de ceteris vocibus trium angelorum reads 'because of the remaining voices of the three angels' (omitting 'of the trumpet' found in Greek) and retains the past-sequence imperfect erant tuba canituri ('were about to sound the trumpet') within the eagle's cry.
notes.9:3: The Clementine Vulgate explicitly reads de fumo putei ('from the smoke of the pit'), specifying 'of the pit' where most Greek manuscripts read simply 'from the smoke.'
notes.9:11: The closing clause latine habens nomen Exterminans ('having in Latin the name Exterminans,' meaning 'Destroyer' or 'Exterminator') is a distinctive Vulgate addition absent from the Greek text.
notes.9:13: Vulgate ante oculos Dei ('before the eyes of God') is a distinctive reading where the Greek text reads simply 'before God.'
notes.9:16: Latin vicies millies dena millia literally means 'twenty thousand times ten thousand,' which equals two hundred million.
notes.9:20: Latin poenitentiam agere (here and in 9:21) is the standard Vulgate idiom for 'to repent,' literally meaning 'to perform repentance/penance.'
notes.10:2: The Clementine Vulgate uses the diminutive libellum ("small book") only in 10:2, whereas 10:8, 9, and 10 all use librum ("book").
notes.10:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads simply manum suam ("his hand"), omitting the word "right" found in Greek manuscripts.
notes.10:6: Literally "time will be no longer" (tempus non erit amplius); in context, the oath is commonly understood to mean that there will be no further delay before the seventh trumpet.
notes.10:7: The Vulgate reads per servos suos prophetas ("through His servants the prophets"), whereas the Greek has an accusative object ("announced the good news to his servants the prophets").
notes.10:11: The Clementine Vulgate has singular dixit ("he said") and orders gentibus, et populis ("nations and peoples"), whereas critical Greek texts read plural "they said" and place "peoples" before "nations."
notes.11:3: Latin dabo duobus testibus meis ("I will give to My two witnesses") preserves the elliptic biblical construction without an explicit direct object, denoting God's granting of a prophetic commission.
notes.11:8: The Clementine Vulgate uses plural corpora ("bodies") and plateis ("streets") and adds the verb jacebunt ("will lie"), whereas critical Greek texts read singular "corpse" and "street" without a verb; likewise 11:9 has plural corpora and monumentis ("tombs") and places tribubus ("tribes") before populis ("peoples").
notes.11:13: Literally nomina hominum septem millia ("seven thousand names of people/men"), a biblical idiom referring to counted individuals.
notes.11:15: The Clementine Vulgate distinctly specifies hujus mundi ("of this world") and closes the acclamation with Amen, both absent from standard Greek editions.
notes.11:19: The Clementine Vulgate lists four phenomena (flashes of lightning, voices, an earthquake, and great hail), omitting the "thunders" present in Greek manuscripts.
notes.12:4: The Vulgate reads filium ("son"), whereas the Greek has teknon ("child").
notes.12:5: The Vulgate renders the verb with recturus erat ("was to rule/govern"), rather than the Greek image of "shepherding" with an iron rod.
notes.12:17: The Clementine Vulgate includes the title Christi ("Jesus Christ"), whereas critical Greek texts read simply "Jesus."
notes.12:18: Following the Clementine Vulgate versification and third-person verb stetit ("he stood"), this verse concludes chapter 12 with the dragon standing on the sand of the sea (unlike the Textus Receptus first-person "I stood" at 13:1).
notes.13:2: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'his power and great authority' (virtutem suam, et potestatem magnam), omitting 'and his throne' found in the Greek text.
notes.13:8: The Vulgate uses the past tense adoraverunt ('worshiped') where the Greek has a future tense, and unambiguously links ab origine mundi ('from the beginning of the world') to the Lamb who was killed.
notes.13:10: The Vulgate reads Qui in captivitatem duxerit ('Whoever leads into captivity'), matching the parallel retribution of the sword clause, whereas modern critical Greek editions read 'If anyone is destined for captivity.'
notes.13:16: The Vulgate uses the future tense faciet ('will cause') and habere caracterem ('to have a mark'), where the Greek uses the present tense and 'that they be given a mark.'
notes.14:3: The Vulgate reads dicere canticum ('recite [or say] the song') where the Greek text has 'learn the song.'
notes.14:5: The Vulgate includes ante thronum Dei ('before the throne of God'), a phrase omitted in most modern critical Greek editions.
notes.14:7: The Vulgate distinctively reads Dominum ('the Lord') and honorem ('honor'), where the Greek text has 'God' and 'glory.'
notes.14:10: The Latin phrase mistum est mero (literally 'mixed with pure/undiluted wine') preserves the Greek oxymoron for wine poured out at full strength without water.
notes.14:13: The Clementine Vulgate places Amodo ('from now on') at the opening of the Spirit's response (Amodo jam dicit Spiritus, omitting 'Yes') rather than at the end of the beatitude as in most Greek editions.
notes.15:3: The Vulgate reads Rex saeculorum ('King of the ages'), aligning with the Greek variant aionon rather than 'King of the nations' (ethnon) or 'King of the saints' (hagion).
notes.15:4: The Vulgate translates Greek hosios ('holy') with pius ('merciful' or 'devout/gracious,' standard in Christian Latin when applied to God), and renders doxasei ('glorify') with magnificabit ('magnify').
notes.15:8: The Vulgate reads a majestate Dei ('from the majesty of God'), where the Greek text has 'from the glory of God.'
notes.16:5: The Clementine Vulgate reads 'qui es, et qui eras sanctus' ('who are and who were holy', without an article corresponding to the Greek title 'the Holy One') and uses the relative pronoun 'qui' ('who have judged') rather than the Greek conjunction 'because.'
notes.16:7: The Vulgate reads 'alterum ab altari' ('another from the altar'), whereas Greek manuscripts present the altar itself as speaking.
notes.16:8: The Vulgate reads both 'æstu' ('heat') and 'et igni' ('and with fire'), expanding the Greek expression 'to scorch people with fire.'
notes.16:12: The Vulgate uses the active verb 'siccavit' ('dried up'), making the sixth angel the subject, whereas the Greek uses a passive verb ('its water was dried up').
notes.16:16: The Clementine Vulgate reads the future tense 'congregabit' ('he will gather'), contrasting with the past tense in the Greek text and some Latin manuscripts ('congregavit').
